---
title: "What's new"
description: "New charts, topics and features on Ireland by Numbers, and the latest data from each source."
---

New charts, topics and features are listed here, newest first. Corrections are listed separately on the [Corrections](corrections.qmd) page.

## Changes to the site

**17 November 2026.** A new [Energy](energy/index.qmd) topic, covering [renewable energy and electricity](energy/renewables.qmd) and [energy imports, electricity prices and demand](energy/supply.qmd).

**17 November 2026.** A new [Gender equality](gender/index.qmd) topic, covering [the EU Gender Equality Index](gender/equality-index.qmd), [work, pay and care](gender/work-and-pay.qmd), and [women in politics and business](gender/leadership.qmd).

**17 November 2026.** Two new topics. [Poverty and inequality](poverty/index.qmd) covers [poverty and deprivation](poverty/rates.qmd), [who is most affected](poverty/who.qmd), [child poverty](poverty/child-poverty.qmd) and [income inequality](poverty/inequality.qmd). [Childhood](childhood/index.qmd) covers [children in Ireland](childhood/children.qmd) and [children's health](childhood/health.qmd). The [data centres](ai/data-centres.qmd) page now maps planning applications for data centres by county. Figures across the site are now checked for updates every Friday.

**16 November 2026.** A new [Artificial intelligence](ai/index.qmd) topic, covering [data centres](ai/data-centres.qmd) and [how businesses and people use AI](ai/ai-use.qmd).

**16 November 2026.** Ten new charts comparing Ireland with Northern Ireland, on population, age, fertility, place of birth, general health, home ownership, household income, cross-border commuting, travel to work and qualifications, mostly from tables the CSO and NISRA publish jointly.

**16 November 2026.** Twelve new charts comparing Ireland with the other EU countries, on unemployment, living standards, poverty, inflation, price levels, house prices, government debt, road deaths, fertility, people born abroad, health spending and early school leaving.

**16 November 2026.** A new [Transport](transport/index.qmd) topic, covering [road safety](transport/road-safety.qmd), [walking, cycling and other ways to travel](transport/travel.qmd), [public transport](transport/public-transport.qmd) and [cars](transport/cars.qmd).

**16 November 2026.** A new [Public finances](public-finances/index.qmd) topic, covering tax and revenue, government spending, and the surplus, deficit and debt. New pages on [crime by type of offence](crime/types.qmd), [crime by Garda division](crime/divisions.qmd), [the health service](health/health-service.qmd), [energy and food prices](cost-of-living/energy-and-food.qmd), [births, deaths and marriages](population/births-deaths-marriages.qmd) and [homelessness](housing/homelessness.qmd).

**14 November 2026.** New Education pages on [pupils in primary and secondary schools](education/pupils.qmd), [primary school class sizes](education/class-sizes.qmd), [the Leaving Certificate](education/leaving-cert.qmd) and [third-level education](education/third-level.qmd).

**14 November 2026.** Eleven new county maps, covering disposable income, house prices, new homes, renting, people born abroad, Irish speakers, working from home, driving to work, distance to a GP and to a hospital emergency department, and forest cover. Each county page now shows how the county compares with the others on each of these.

**13 November 2026.** County pages, with the population of each county at every census and the average rent on new tenancies. A weekly chart of the week on the homepage. Key facts at the top of each topic page. New pages on [how the figures are chosen and checked](methods.qmd), a [glossary](glossary.qmd) and a [corrections log](corrections.qmd). Each chart's page now shows when its source was last updated, links to the original table, and has a link that can be shared with a preview image.

**13 November 2026.** The first charts, covering population, housing, the cost of living, the economy and work, and crime, from Central Statistics Office tables. The Education section shows who runs every primary school, from [Fianaise](https://fianaise.ie).

## Latest data
